_meta.indication: Vyvanse is indicated for the treatment of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD); indicated for use in children aged 6 to 12 years.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing three fixed doses of NRP104 (30mg, 50mg, or 70mg) vs. placebo, conducted at 64 centers in the U.S.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients between 6 to 12 years of age with a DSM-IV-TR diagnosis of ADHD.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline of the ADHD Rating Scale (ADHD-RS Version IV) total score at the last post-randomization treatment week (LOCF).
pivotal_trials.result: All three doses were superior to placebo on change in ADHD-RS total score: placebo-adjusted LS mean -15.58 (30 mg), -17.21 (50 mg), -20.49 (70 mg); each p<0.0001 vs placebo.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, three-treatment, three-period, cross-over study in a laboratory classroom setting evaluating NRP104 (30, 50, or 70 mg), Adderall XR, and placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric patients with ADHD (mean age 9.1 years).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Average of the SKAMP Deportment Scores (SKAMP-DS) across the treatment assessment day, rated by the investigator.
pivotal_trials.result: NRP104 LS mean SKAMP-DS 0.8 vs placebo 1.7 (difference -0.9), p<0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse events (>=5% and twice placebo) were decreased appetite (39% vs 4%), insomnia (19% vs 3%), upper abdominal pain (12% vs 6%), irritability (10% vs 0%), weight decreased (9% vs 1%), and vomiting (9% vs 4%). Ten percent (21/218) of Vyvanse-treated patients discontinued due to adverse events vs 1% (1/72) on placebo.
target_moa: Lisdexamfetamine dimesylate is a prodrug of d-amphetamine; after oral administration it is hydrolyzed to active dextroamphetamine, and the intact prodrug is pharmacologically inactive and does not bind the norepinephrine and dopamine reuptake sites.

boxed_warning.content: Amphetamines have a high potential for abuse; prolonged administration may lead to drug dependence and should be prescribed/dispensed sparingly. Misuse of amphetamine may cause sudden death and serious cardiovascular adverse events.

advisory_committee.vote: This submission was not presented to the Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee.

summary.text: Vyvanse (lisdexamfetamine dimesylate), a prodrug of d-amphetamine, was submitted as a 505(b) NDA received December 6, 2005 with a Standard review designation. It was approved via the full (non-accelerated) pathway for ADHD after two approvable letters, with a deferred PREA pediatric study required for ages 13 to 17.
